model: Versati heat pump water heater (wired-controller Modbus RTU, protocol V1.5)
applies_to: Gree Versati air-to-water heat pumps through the BMS port of the wired controller, per 'Modbus Protocol (V1.5) for the Versati Heat Pump Water Heater'. The document itself does not name a generation or refrigerant; the distributor files it as the R32 Versati III protocol.
summary: The Versati wired controller has a two-wire RS-485 BMS port that answers Modbus RTU, so up to 255 heat pumps can sit on one line. Holding registers (words) carry on/off, mode, water and room setpoints, temperature limits, power and current limits, unit status and compressor frequency; coils (bits) carry function switches (timers, quiet mode, weather compensation, disinfection, holiday) and indoor, outdoor and inverter fault and state flags.

addressing.note: Registers are words numbered from 0 and coils are bits numbered from 0 (Bit 0 = Byte0.0). Word n is holding register n and Bit n is coil n on the wire; the protocol's example frames agree (read from word 1 sends 00 01, read from coil 5 sends 00 05).

source.title: Modbus Protocol (V1.5) for the Versati Heat Pump Water Heater
source.pages: pp. 5-7 hardware and address setting, pp. 8-11 frame format and examples, pp. 11-12 precautions, pp. 12-18 words, pp. 19-23 bits

notes: Gree does not appear to host this protocol publicly; the link is an unaltered copy of Gree's document in the Ukrainian distributor Kiev Climate's manual library, filed there under Versati III as 'R32_Versati Modbus V1.5'. Page headers inside still read 'V1.1' while the cover says V1.5.

Every word is printed as an unsigned integer with transmission value = actual value. Words whose printed range goes below 0 °C are left out because the document gives no rule for coding negative values: settings 14 (T-Eheater), 15 (T-Other switch on) and 18 (Lower AT-Heat), and all sensor readings 118-131 (outdoor, discharge, defrost, suction, economizer, discharge pressure, water out/in, optional water sensor, tank, remote room, gas pipe and liquid pipe temperatures).
Reserved words and bits are left out, as are bits 99, 100, 177, 178 and 184, which are named but have no access type printed.
Word 42 uses 0xAA for on and 0x55 for off, not 1/0. Word 43 is sent as kW x 10.
Several limits differ between high-temperature and low-temperature units (words 10 and 21); the description quotes both ranges.

integration.summary: Wire the BMS port of the wired controller to RS-485, set a unique address, then read words 117-143 and coils 64-191 for status and faults, and write word 42 (0xAA/0x55), word 2 (mode) and the setpoint words.
integration.enable: On the wired controller press COMMISSION, then FUNCTION, page to 'Address', set the BMS address and press OK. The address must not be 0 or 126 and must match the address the BMS sends.
quirks: Read with function 0x03 and write with 0x10 (words); read with 0x01 and write with 0x0F (bits). Single-write functions 0x05/0x06 are not listed.
Broadcast (address 0) is accepted for writes only.
BMS and Gree long-distance monitoring have equal control; the most recent command wins.
setup: 9600 bit/s, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit.
Controller BMS terminal: 1 = B, 2 = A (two-wire, twisted pair).
gotchas: Change the mode only while the unit is off; mode writes while running may be ignored.
Hot-water related modes and functions are ignored when no water tank is configured, and cooling modes are ignored on heating-only units.
After commanding disinfection, check word 135 for its state.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
